paragraphs: A village in India was celebrating with a grand procession, and the star of the show was a beautifully decorated elephant. Everyone was thrilled. Five blind men in the crowd could not see it, so they asked to touch the elephant and find out what it was like. They were allowed to.

Walking home afterwards, they started comparing notes. One said the elephant was exactly like a wall. Another disagreed: it was like a rope. A third insisted it was a snake, he had felt it himself. The fourth declared it was like a pillow.
Voices rose, tempers flared, and soon the five were actually fighting.

Then a man who could see came by and asked what the trouble was. When he heard, he laughed kindly. Every one of them was right, he told them. One had touched the side, which felt like a wall; another the tail, like a rope; another the trunk, like a snake; and another the feet, like a pillow. They had simply met the same elephant from different points. There was nothing to fight about.
learn: Most arguments, whether about religion, politics or a group project, happen because each side holds one true piece of a bigger picture. Before you fight, ask what the other person has touched that you haven't.
